content:
The long-awaited new Apple TV 4K arrives late to the party, with the market originally expecting it to debut last fall. However, with Siri AI finally ready to go, all signs point to a new Apple TV 4K on the horizon — most likely unveiled at the September 9 event. Here are the rumours currently circulating.

Point one: Siri Remote update

Although no details have been revealed, Apple is reportedly preparing an updated Siri Remote for the new Apple TV 4K.

Code leaked from the macOS 26.7 beta appears to confirm the existence of a new Siri Remote. And prior to this leak, Mark Gurman had already reported that the new hardware might come with a "redesigned Apple TV remote".

It doesn't look like there will be any major changes, but hopefully at least a second-generation ultra-wideband chip will be added to support Precision Finding.

Point two: Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features

Siri AI is expected to be the main selling point of the new Apple TV and other new home products.

So far, Apple has not revealed whether the new assistant features will land on the Apple TV 4K or HomePod. But mounting evidence suggests tvOS 27 will include Siri AI — and most likely only support new hardware.

We also have a good chance of seeing other Apple Intelligence features, such as an enhanced search experience.

Point three: Next-generation A-series chip

The current Apple TV uses the A15 Bionic chip, first introduced in 2021. The good news is that the new model is expected to see a significant performance boost.

The new device will feature a more powerful A-series chip to support AI capabilities.

Rumours suggest the new chip could be the A17 Pro or A18. However, most of these reports surfaced before Siri AI was announced. It wouldn't be surprising if Apple opted for an even more powerful A19 or A20 chip instead.

Point four: N1 wireless chip

Live commentary from Doug

Ideally, it should be able to replace older HomePod devices and support Siri AI capabilities.

Second, it should have a built-in microphone so it can receive Siri AI commands without using the remote.

Finally, it should offer the long-promised universal TV remote functionality (long stalled by partners like Netflix), and allow us to search for new shows across all streaming services (including cable TV providers).

Netflix's library data is public, so Siri AI can search across all the media content I have access to. The Apple TV should become a truly universal set-top box.

In addition, AirPlay should have long supported connecting multiple HomePods for a true home theatre setup, including auto-calibrated Atmos sound.

The N1 wireless chip, reportedly debuting in the iPhone 17, is also expected to feature in the new Apple TV 4K.

By adding the N1 chip, Apple will bring Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support to the Apple TV, as well as Thread networking support.

By comparison, the existing Apple TV hardware is already four years old and only supports Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.

What features would you like to see on the new Apple TV 4K? Feel free to share in the comments section.
